limitations:
### 2.3. Limitations of Existing Approaches

Table.​ 1summarizes existing approaches along both dimensions; none covers both efficiently.
Filesystem-only tools (Git stash/branch (Yang et al., 2024), shutil.copytree, Docker commit, Btrfs/LVM snapshots) version files but discard process memory, forcing a restart and replay.
VM snapshots (Firecracker (Agache et al., 2020)) dump the whole guest’s memory and device state but not the block device, so a consistent filesystem rollback needs a separate block snapshot; and the memory dump is VM-granular, capturing kernel, slab, and daemon pages irrelevant to the agent.
Agent sandboxes either lack event-level coupled rollback altogether (DSec (DeepSeek-AI, 2026) only replays cached outputs from a write-ahead log, with no arbitrary rollback) or, like E2B (E2B, 2026), offer coupled, transparent C/R only through a VM-granular pause/snapshot at seconds scale ( {\sim}4  s per GiB of RAM) that grows with total memory, far too slow for the high-frequency, on-critical-path rollback tree search demands.
DeltaBox instead manages the coupled physical (filesystem, memory) state as a single, atomically consistent unit at millisecond-scale overhead (§​ 4.4).

Figure 2. Design Overview. DeltaBox uses diff-based checkpoint/restore (deltaCheckpoint and deltaRestore) to enable millisecond-level checkpoint/rollback. The agent worker runs inside the sandbox, so every step is C/R-protected and can be rolled back promptly when needed.

### 2.4. Design Requirements

Based on the above analysis, we identify four key requirements for an efficient agent sandbox:

R1 

Millisecond-level coupled checkpoint/restore. Both filesystem and process state must be saved and restored jointly at millisecond scale.

R2 

Write amplification proportional to actual changes. Storage overhead must scale with the agent’s actual modifications, not working directory size.

R3 

 O(1) arbitrary rollback. Support rollback to any historical checkpoint in constant time.

R4 

Agent transparency. The coupled checkpoint/restore should be mostly invisible to the agent, i.e., no code changes, no forced restarts, and no context loss.

## 3. System Overview

This paper presents DeltaBox, a new agent sandbox that satisfies the four requirements.
Following our key insight that consecutive checkpoints differ only marginally (§​ 1), DeltaBox duplicates only the inter-checkpoint changes rather than the whole state.

Fig.​ 2sketches the resulting end-to-end workflow.
The agent worker runs inside the sandbox, so every search step is C/R-protected.
Concurrently with each LLM round-trip, the StateManager issues a deltaCheckpoint that persists only the delta of the coupled (memory, filesystem) state for that step.
A rollback is a deltaRestore: it switches the overlay layer stack to the target in one shot, then reconstructs the target process memory by forking a warm template (on hit) or loading the CRIU image chain (on miss).
